name: Sick of It All
label: Revelation
lede: Two brothers from Queens, one borrowed basement, a seven-inch that's been repressed in a rainbow of vinyl for almost forty years, and a band that carried New York hardcore onto MTV and around the planet without ever sanding the edges off.

eras.title: Scared to death at the Right Track Inn
eras.text: Lou Koller and Pete Koller built the band in their parents' Queens basement in the summers the folks were away, soaking up metal and hardcore in equal parts. Within a year they'd gone from a nervous opening slot on Long Island to the CBGB Sunday matinees and the third release on a brand-new label called Revelation.

years.cap: First show, Right Track Inn, Long Island
years.h: First show: Long Island, a month of practice, a [[Cause for Alarm|1940001f-3270-4d87-9501-eb243d5f9f50]] cover to close
years.p: [[Craig Setari|3908d895-a1af-42a7-b86b-93a3074057ee]], then playing with [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], got them on a Right Track Inn bill with Youth of Today, [[Straight Ahead|1fd60d7c-dc35-44f5-9162-4113b6ca4a69]] and Crippled Youth. They'd rehearsed for about a month, ran the originals first, then closed with a Cause for Alarm cover that lit the room up.
years.xp:
The band didn't feel ready and said so for decades after. The plan was simple: get the unknown songs out of the way, then finish on something the crowd already loved, and let that carry them off stage.

The man who booked the gig, Setari, would end up in the band seven years later and stay for the next three decades.

years.h: The rhythm section that stuck (for a while)
years.p: After the first show the original drummer and bassist were out. [[Rich Cipriano|fe1b3bb1-f4b1-4359-b308-30247a89e9d8]] took bass and [[Armand Majidi|5835deec-ae60-4ac0-888e-5b5e70270d0f]] took the drums, the line-up that made the early records.
A self-titled demo, then regular spots on the CBGB hardcore matinees, where the band's reputation got built one pit at a time.

A thousand hand-numbered black copies on the first press, no Rev logo on the A-side art. It also gave the world, by accident, the dragon that would crawl back onto seven of their studio albums, lifted in spirit from a Greg Irons tattoo flash sheet.
years.xp: Revelation has kept the record alive ever since: a numbered red second press, 300 black copies for a Gilman Street record convention, a 33 rpm run, a 10th-anniversary repress in 1997, then clear vinyl for Record Store Day 2010 and a string of colors after that.

eras.title: Seven albums on paper, a revolving door in the van
eras.text: A seven-album deal with Relativity put them on the road with everyone from Agnostic Front to Bad Brains to Exodus. The records got bigger while the rhythm section kept changing underneath them, and for one EP the band printed photos of members who were already gone.

years.h: Relativity signs them for seven albums
years.p: The Koller brothers go from a Rev single to a long-term deal, and start opening for [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]], [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]] and, for five East Coast dates, thrash band Exodus.
The debut LP on Relativity. Kerrang! would later say it helped change what the world meant by New York hardcore. The video for Injustice System left Lou unhappy with how it turned out.
Headlining runs, then support on Bad Brains' Quickness tour with [[Leeway|121193a5-cb8b-4182-968c-8ba607856fa2]], including two weeks on the West Coast.

[[Max Capshaw|74d0e618-1149-46b2-898b-7169b7f9819d]] covers the drums. Majidi is back in time for a national run with [[D.R.I.|95f6e954-8bed-4f8e-a53e-d155bb6f7ace]], and Capshaw is out; Lou's verdict later was that he was too young.

years.h: Both halves of the rhythm section walk
years.p: Before an [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]] tour, Cipriano and Majidi are gone. [[Eddie Coen|6c1ec806-8c9e-4a6f-be2f-ae0d940e0f30]] and [[Eric Komst|bba140d0-01c1-4a77-a596-30f376822207]] step in. Coen soon leaves for the Cycle Sluts from Hell, and Komst is eventually fired.

years.h: We Stand Alone EP, with ghosts in the liner notes
years.p: Coen and Komst are pictured anyway, a way of telling fans the band was still standing. That same year they're on the New Titans on the Bloc tour with [[Sepultura|1d93c839-22e7-4f76-ad84-d27039efc048]], [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]] and Sacred Reich. By the time the next album is recorded, Majidi and Cipriano are back.
Second Relativity LP, followed by a spring run through Europe and a winter tour of the continent.

eras.title: Hardcore on Headbangers Ball
eras.text: With Craig Setari on bass the line-up locked in for good, and East West took the band to a major. Scratch the Surface put a New York hardcore video into MTV rotation, something nobody had seen coming, and sent the band to Japan, South America and New Zealand.

years.p: The guy who booked their first show replaces Cipriano. The Kollers, Majidi and Setari are the line-up for the next thirty-plus years. By year's end: shows in Japan, a live album (Live in a World Full of Hate) and a deal with East West.

Their first album to chart, debuting at No. 67 in Germany. The title-track video premiered on MTV's Headbangers Ball on December 10, and Step Down went into rotation, a thing that would have sounded absurd at a CBGB matinee a few years earlier.
years.xp:
Vice's Mike Hill called it the album that took NYHC worldwide, turning the band into the closest thing hardcore had to a household name. Step Down even turned up on Beavis and Butt-Head.

The touring was relentless: two weeks with [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]], a November run supporting [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]] and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]], ten shows with [[Black Train Jack|be939900-e334-431e-b85a-c62f4ec3bf60]], then the Americas, Europe, Japan and New Zealand.

years.h: Headlining over a young [[Korn|ac865b2e-bba8-4f5a-8756-dd40d5e39f46]], then the first Warped Tour
years.p: A January to March US headline run with Korn, Orange 9mm and Trial, then a slot on the very first Warped Tour.

Their only album for East West's sister label, and the home of set staples Us vs. Them, Busted and Good Lookin' Out. The same year Revelation reissues the 1987 debut on vinyl and CD for its tenth birthday.

eras.title: Fat Mike, Slayer and the long road
eras.text: Off the majors and onto NOFX frontman Fat Mike's Fat Wreck Chords, the band stopped chasing anything but the next show. A crowd in Argentina brought Slayer calling, and by the band's 20th birthday a roster of younger bands was lining up to cover them.

years.h: Call to Arms, first for Fat Wreck Chords
years.p: Signed to Fat Mike's label in 1998, they open with the Potential for a Fall single, then this. Earlier in 1999, [[Slayer|bdacc37b-8633-4bf8-9dd5-4662ee651aec]] members catch a Sick of It All show in Argentina and invite them out; they tour with Slayer and [[Meshuggah|cf8b3b8c-118e-4136-8d1d-c37091173413]] later that year.

years.h: Yours Truly, and the cover Lou blames
years.p: Critics were cooler on it, though District and Blown Away became fan favorites. Lou later suggested the cover art may have hurt the album's reception.
A new label under the Century Media umbrella, and an album critics heard as proof the band hadn't slowed down.

years.h: Twenty years, B.B. King's on 42nd Street
years.p: The anniversary show lands in Times Square, a long way from the Right Track Inn.

years.h: Our Impact Will Be Felt: everybody covers them
years.p: A tribute album with [[Sepultura|1d93c839-22e7-4f76-ad84-d27039efc048]], [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]], [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]], [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]], Bouncing Souls, [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]], [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]] and more taking a swing at the catalog.

eras.title: Thirty years of the wall of death
eras.text: Now on Century Media, the band marked anniversaries the way they marked everything else: by getting in the van. They played whole albums front to back, re-recorded their own history, and in 2020 the brothers finally put it all in a book.

years.h: Based on a True Story, made in Copenhagen
years.p: First album for Century Media, recorded with producer Tue Madsen in Denmark instead of New York.
The same year, at Fun Fun Fun Fest in Austin, they play both Scratch the Surface and Blood, Sweat, and No Tears all the way through.
A hometown anniversary with [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]], in the middle of a world tour for the milestone. When the Smoke Clears, an EP of new songs, follows on November 4.

q: We wanted to show the world what we loved.
years.p: The dragon from the 1987 seven-inch, now in the title. Around this time Lou pushed back on the Kings of New York hardcore tag.
years.xp: Lou's preferred word for the band was ambassadors, not kings. It fit a group that had spent thirty years bringing New York hardcore to Brazil, Japan and German festival fields.

years.p: With touring shut down, Lou and Pete publish The Blood and Sweat: The Story of Sick of It All's Koller Brothers. Decibel called it one of the best books ever written about hardcore.

eras.title: The last fight
eras.text: Forty years in, the band's hardest stretch had nothing to do with labels or line-ups. First Pete sat out a tour for surgery, then Lou's esophageal cancer pulled them off the road, the scene he helped build rallied around him, and in the band's 40th year he died.

years.p: Pete Koller sits out the 2022 European tour to have surgery for a hernia, as Blabbermouth and Wikipedia report. Craig Silverman fills in on guitar, and Pete is back afterward.

years.h: An esophageal tumor, and Europe is called off
years.p: Lou announces he's been diagnosed with esophageal cancer; Rolling Stone ran it as a tumor diagnosis. He starts treatment that summer and the July European dates are cancelled.

years.h: The scene shows up for Lou
years.p: A benefit show with [[Life of Agony|d6ff259a-bbb6-4454-8503-80151da5f2db]], [[Municipal Waste|b5a31e9b-1fa2-45f9-91f5-b3a25fb38038]], [[Crown of Thornz|e7b3e015-81fa-4180-aa7b-7bfcf821209d]] and [[Vision of Disorder|618a18b1-dec3-4c4a-813b-988d9c065722]].

years.h: Cancer free, and ready to get back to it
years.p: Lou announces he's officially cancer free. In August Setari says new music is in the works with shows planned for 2026.
Lou tells fans the cancer has returned, months after he'd been declared clear.

years.src: Blabbermouth · Arrow Lords of Metal · Wikipedia
years.p: Lou describes his treatment as at a stalemate, with the tumors neither growing nor shrinking. Pete says his brother lost 70 pounds during treatment and was put on a feeding tube, as Blabbermouth reported.

years.h: Lou Koller dies in the band's 40th year
years.p: Lou died on July 24 in hospice care in Matawan, New Jersey, after a two-year fight with esophageal cancer, as Wikipedia and the obituaries report. The band announced it to what they called their worldwide hardcore family, noting this would have been Sick of It All's fortieth year. He is survived by his wife Melissa, his daughter and his brother Pete.

years.h: Pete: Lou asked them to keep going
years.p: In an Instagram video Pete says his brother wanted the band to continue after him, and that they're working out how to honor that.
